subject.title: 2026.7.1 startup-migration gate is fatal, but the repair path (`openclaw doctor`) doesn't resolve the conflict — gateway crash-loops with no documented remedy

question: When legacy plugin or health metadata genuinely conflicts with shared SQLite during startup, should Doctor require an explicit authoritative-side choice, or may it automatically back up and retire regenerable legacy sources?
rationale: The existing fail-safe policy preserves true conflicts to avoid silently discarding meaningful metadata, but the new fatal readiness gate makes leaving them unresolved an unusable upgrade path; code evidence cannot choose the intended compatibility policy.

options.title: Guided Doctor Resolution
options.body: Add a backed-up Doctor repair flow that displays each conflict, recommends the safe side when provable, and requires confirmation for ambiguous records before restarting the service.

options.title: SQLite Wins Automatically
options.body: Treat shared SQLite as authoritative for these legacy sources, archive all conflicting files, and document the compatibility tradeoff with focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed
options.body: Retain unresolved conflicts as fatal but replace the no-op Doctor hint with exact supported backup and recovery commands plus visible app/status guidance.

recommendation.title: Guided Doctor Resolution
recommendation.body: Add a backed-up Doctor repair flow that displays each conflict, recommends the safe side when provable, and requires confirmation for ambiguous records before restarting the service.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history covers both the shared migration ownership boundary and the startup lease/readiness recovery behavior that created this policy intersection.
